conversation_context.content: I'm instrumenting a Python agent by hand. How can I attach env='staging' to just one turn in its trace?

Call `set_attributes()` on that turn's `Turn` object while the turn is active. This stamps the attributes on that one span [S1].

```python
import weave

weave.init("[TEAM-NAME]/[PROJECT-NAME]")

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="my-agent"):
    with weave.start_turn(user_message="What is the weather in Tokyo?") as turn:
        turn.set_attributes({"env": "staging"})
```

This pattern follows the docs' example, which sets `env: "production"` on a turn [S1]. Pass a dictionary, with one key or many. The method returns the span, so you can chain calls [S1].

**Things to know**
- **Timing:** Call it while the span is recording, which in Python means inside the `with` block. On a span that hasn't started or has already ended, the call is a no-op and logs a warning [S3].
- **Scope:** `set_attributes()` applies to the single span you call it on. Weave also has a separate way to set conversation-wide attributes that apply to every span a conversation emits [S2]. Avoid that if you want only one turn tagged.
- **Other spans:** `LLM`, `Tool` and `SubAgent` spans have the same method, so you can tag a single tool call instead of the whole turn [S1].
- **Key names:** `env` is a custom key, so Weave stores it as a filterable custom attribute. Keys starting with `weave.` or `gen_ai.` are reserved for built-in fields [S1].
- **Batch logging:** If you log completed activity in a batch with `log_turn` or `log_conversation`, don't call `set_attributes()`. Populate the span object's declared fields directly and pass the object in [S3].

No, you don't need to repeat the metadata on each LLM and tool span. Pass `attributes` once to `startConversation`, and every span in that conversation carries them [S4].

```typescript
import * as weave from 'weave';

await weave.init('[TEAM-NAME]/[PROJECT-NAME]');

const conversation = weave.startConversation({
  agentName: 'my-agent',
  attributes: { env: 'production' },
});
// Every turn, LLM, tool, and sub-agent span in this conversation carries env: 'production'.
```

This is the documented pattern, trimmed to your one key. The docs' version also sets `'weave.integration.name'`, which you don't need [S4].

**Why it works**
- `startConversation` installs the new conversation as the current one, and later `startTurn` calls pick it up automatically [S6].
- `attributes` propagates custom attributes to every span the conversation emits [S5].
- The `TurnInit` reference says a turn's attributes are normally seeded from the conversation through `startConversation({ attributes })`. A rootless `startTurn({ attributes })` with no conversation is the exception [S7].

- Use your own custom key like `env`. Avoid keys under the reserved `gen_ai.*` and `weave.*` prefixes. Set built-in fields such as agent name or model through their typed parameters, not through `attributes` [S4].

- Without a conversation, you would need `startTurn({ attributes })` on a rootless turn [S7]. That is the case where you'd set them on the turn yourself.
- Per-span `setAttributes()` is still available on each span for span-specific values [S4].

# Set attributes and events on agent spans

> Attach custom attributes and record events on agent spans (Turn, LLM, Tool, and SubAgent) to filter and analyze agent activity in Weave.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/attributes-and-events).

When you instrument an agent with the Weave SDK, each span object (`Turn`, `LLM`, `Tool`, and `SubAgent`) exposes methods to attach custom metadata. Use these methods to stamp contextual information such as user IDs, tenants, experiment names, or environment labels onto agent spans, then filter and group agent activity by that metadata in the Weights & Biases UI.

This metadata comes in two forms:

* **Attributes**: Key-value properties of a span as a whole. Use `set_attributes()` (Python) or `setAttributes()` (TypeScript) to stamp attributes on a single span, or set conversation-wide attributes that apply to every span a conversation emits.
* **Events**: Point-in-time markers that occur during a span's lifetime, such as a permission prompt or a lifecycle transition. Use `add_event()` (Python) or `addEvent()` (TypeScript).

These methods mirror the [OpenTelemetry (OTel) span API](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-spans/): `set_attributes` mirrors OTel's `Span.set_attributes`, and `add_event` mirrors OTel's `Span.add_event`. The Weave SDK emits OTel spans and stores all attributes, so they remain queryable in Weave.

all_read_evidence.text:
## When you can set attributes

Set attributes while the span is recording, that is, after the span starts and before it ends. In Python, this is inside the `with` block. In TypeScript, this is after `start*()` and before `end()`.

If you call `set_attributes()`, or its TypeScript equivalent on a span that hasn't started yet or has already ended, the call is a no-op and logs a warning that names the fix.

The call is silent (no warning) only when OTel isn't installed or Weave is disabled.

> [!TIP]
>
> To attach attributes when logging completed agent activity in a single batch rather than during live execution, populate the span object's declared fields directly and pass the object to `log_turn` or `log_conversation`. See [Log agent activity in batches](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents-batch.md).

No, you don't need to repeat the metadata on each LLM and tool span. Pass `attributes` once to `startConversation`, and every span in that conversation carries them [S4].

```typescript
import * as weave from 'weave';

await weave.init('[TEAM-NAME]/[PROJECT-NAME]');

const conversation = weave.startConversation({
  agentName: 'my-agent',
  attributes: { env: 'production' },
});
// Every turn, LLM, tool, and sub-agent span in this conversation carries env: 'production'.
```

This is the documented pattern, trimmed to your one key. The docs' version also sets `'weave.integration.name'`, which you don't need [S4].

**Why it works**
- `startConversation` installs the new conversation as the current one, and later `startTurn` calls pick it up automatically [S6].
- `attributes` propagates custom attributes to every span the conversation emits [S5].

```python

    with weave.start_turn(user_message="What is the weather in Tokyo?") as turn:
```

## When you can set attributes

Set attributes while the span is recording, that is, after the span starts and before it ends. In Python, this is inside the `with` block. In TypeScript, this is after `start*()` and before `end()`.

If you call `set_attributes()`, or its TypeScript equivalent on a span that hasn't started yet or has already ended, the call is a no-op and logs a warning that names the fix.

The call is silent (no warning) only when OTel isn't installed or Weave is disabled.

> [!TIP]
>
> To attach attributes when logging completed agent activity in a single batch rather than during live execution, populate the span object's declared fields directly and pass the object to `log_turn` or `log_conversation`. See [Log agent activity in batches](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents-batch.md).

### <kbd>method</kbd> `record`

```python theme={"system"}
record(
    messages: 'list[Message] | None' = None,
    system_instructions: 'list[str] | None' = None,
    agent_name: 'str | None' = None,
    model: 'str | None' = None,
    agent_id: 'str | None' = None,
    agent_description: 'str | None' = None,
    agent_version: 'str | None' = None
```

Set multiple turn fields in one call.

Collapses the per-field assignments a manually-instrumented agent otherwise makes on a turn (`system_instructions`, `agent_id`, ...) into a single keyword call. ## When you can set attributes

Set attributes while the span is recording, that is, after the span starts and before it ends. In Python, this is inside the `with` block. In TypeScript, this is after `start*()` and before `end()`.

all_read_evidence.text:
## When you can set attributes

Set attributes while the span is recording, that is, after the span starts and before it ends. In Python, this is inside the `with` block. In TypeScript, this is after `start*()` and before `end()`.

If you call `set_attributes()`, or its TypeScript equivalent on a span that hasn't started yet or has already ended, the call is a no-op and logs a warning that names the fix.

The call is silent (no warning) only when OTel isn't installed or Weave is disabled.

> [!TIP]
>
> To attach attributes when logging completed agent activity in a single batch rather than during live execution, populate the span object's declared fields directly and pass the object to `log_turn` or `log_conversation`. See [Log agent activity in batches](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents-batch.md).
